papers.title: Weekly set volume and muscle thickness in trained men: a randomised trial
papers.quickTakeaway: Thirty-two trained men trained chest at two weekly set counts for 10 weeks. The higher volume produced more thickness, with wide individual variation.
papers.whatTheyStudied: Two weekly set counts for the chest over 10 weeks in trained men.
papers.whatTheyFound: Thickness rose more in the higher-volume group, though individual responses varied widely.
papers.forLifters: In resistance-trained men over 10 weeks, more weekly sets may add more size, but the spread between people was large.
limitations: One muscle and one measurement site.
Ten weeks is short for a size outcome.
A single trial rather than a body of evidence.

papers.title: Self-reported sleep and grip strength in a national survey
papers.quickTakeaway: In a survey of adults, shorter self-reported sleep was associated with lower grip strength.
papers.whatTheyStudied: A cross-sectional survey linking reported sleep duration to grip strength.
papers.whatTheyFound: Shorter sleep was associated with lower grip strength.
papers.forLifters: In these surveyed adults, sleep and strength moved together; the design cannot say which way round.
limitations: Cross-sectional, so no time order can be established.
Grip strength is an indirect measure of training strength.

papers.title: A pooled analysis of proximity to failure and hypertrophy
papers.quickTakeaway: Pooling trials of training to failure against stopping short found little difference in growth when sets were taken reasonably close.
papers.whatTheyStudied: A pooled analysis of trials comparing sets taken to failure with sets stopped short of it.
papers.whatTheyFound: Growth differences were small once sets were within a few repetitions of failure.
papers.forLifters: In the trained participants these trials studied, stopping a rep or two short may cost little growth.
papers.participants: Participants pooled across the included trials, mostly resistance-trained.
limitations: The included trials measured size in different ways.
How close 'close to failure' was differed between trials.
